name: Thai Peanut Noodles
steps: Cook or soak the rice noodles as their package directs until flexible and just tender. Drain, rinse briefly with cool water and shake off excess moisture; overcooked noodles will break when tossed.

Whisk peanut butter, lime juice, soy sauce, sesame oil, brown sugar, grated ginger and garlic. Add the measured 140 ml warm water in stages, whisking until the sauce is smooth, creamy and pourable. Taste for a clear balance of salty, sour and sweet.

Cut red bell pepper into thin strips and carrot and cucumber into fine matchsticks. Slice spring onion, pick coriander leaves, chop roasted peanuts and cut lime into wedges. Keep these vegetables raw so they contrast with the soft noodles.

Place drained noodles in a large bowl. Add about two-thirds of the sauce and lift with tongs until strands are evenly coated. If noodles absorb the sauce, add a little more, reserving enough to drizzle at serving.

Divide among four bowls. Arrange pepper, carrot and cucumber over the noodles; scatter spring onion, coriander and chopped peanuts. Drizzle remaining sauce and serve with lime wedges to squeeze at the table.
tips: This is a Thai-inspired peanut noodle bowl, not a claim of traditional pad Thai. The reviewed photo shows peanut-coated rice noodles with red pepper, carrot, cucumber, scallion, coriander, peanuts and lime.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
